summary: The complete paper and publisher supplements are accessible. Every one of the 13,266 gene rows in Table S2 repeats six result fields from a different-labelled polyadenylation site in Table S1, including the fields for both printed adjusted-P discoveries at the paper’s 0.10 cutoff. The original gene-level fit is needed to establish the effects and inference for this contrast.

manualReview.summary: Recovered gene table repeats site-level statistics under different gene labels
manualReview.note: The deposited WTTS site matrix and family SOFT match their registered source hashes. The university-hosted published article and all six publisher supplements are accessible. The paper identifies S2 as the gene-summed result for the diet experiment. Across 9,395 unique gene-ID-supported pairs, the printed S2 log2 fold changes agree in direction with registered edgeR-QL for 4,724 genes. Every S2 result tuple matches a unique S1 site with another symbol or no symbol. The 9,395 pairs therefore document the problem with interpreting the printed columns. A separate HFD-minus-chow calculation from S2’s normalized library values agrees in direction for 8,291 pairs. Those descriptive changes do not recover the original fitted coefficients or tests.
reviewFlags: The publisher and first-author archive give the same S2 worksheet values. A corrected, gene-ID-keyed result is needed before assigning S2 coefficients, P values or adjusted P values to genes.
The paper reports 73 genes at raw P < 0.01. S2 has 135 printed rows at that cutoff. Its two adjusted-P values below 0.10 repeat those for S1 sites 10545 and 3502.

Article sections 2.3 and 2.4 respectively describe pooled RNA and a control technical replicate, and four individual libraries per arm. GEO identifies eight distinct BioSamples. The fitted animal-to-library map remains unclear.

verificationReview.reason: The full labelled gene table is public. Its base mean, log2 fold change, standard error, test statistic, P and adjusted P on every row are identical to those for one S1 site with a different label. Direct comparison of the printed fields and separate comparison of the normalized expression columns cannot establish the original gene-level fitted results. Author-concordance-v2 remains unassessed for genuine gene effects.
verificationReview.nextStep: Can you provide the original gene-ID-keyed, 36-day HFD-versus-chow WTTS gene-summed DESeq/DESeq2 output with log2 fold changes, raw P, adjusted P and fitted sample IDs, and explain why S2 columns M:R reproduce S1 site statistics for different gene labels? Which animals or pools contributed to each fitted library, and did the fit include a control technical replicate?

comparabilityReview.basis: The unchanged registered gene-summed edgeR-QL table was compared with the full S2 worksheet as printed. The numerical pairings diagnose row attribution, with a separate descriptive check of normalized expression on its supplied scale.
comparabilityReview.reference: Brutman et al., PMID 29391168, Supplementary Table S2 Sheet1 A:R. Table S1 T:Y identifies site-level result tuples. The author’s Chapter 3 archive preserves the same worksheet values. S3 gives site counts, S4–S5 characterize selected sites, and Figure 5 used an independent 40-day qPCR cohort.

cohort.note: GEO, ENA, the registered sample sheet and the two diet groups support eight male Long-Evans hypothalamic libraries, four per arm at 36 days. Workbook identifiers differ from GEO titles. The paper describes pooling and a control technical replicate in one section and individual library preparations in the next. BioSample identity alone cannot resolve the fitted biological units.

contrast.note: The same 36-day HFD/DIO versus standard-chow exposure is stated in both sources. HFD is case in the registered model. S2 E:H are control and I:L are HFD. The authors describe increased expression under HFD as positive.

features.note: All 13,266 S2 gene IDs are unique. Exact one-to-one symbols supported by the deposited gene ID yield 9,395 registered pairs. Twenty repeated S2 symbols account for 40 excluded rows. Every printed M:R tuple maps uniquely to a different-labelled S1 site, and together those sites have IDs 1 through 13,266.

effects.note: For literal S2 log2 fold changes versus registered effects, Pearson r = −0.008020, Spearman rho = −0.004849, and 4,724 of 9,395 nonzero signs agree. These metrics have no confirmed gene-level interpretation. Subtracting control from HFD mean normalized expression (E:L) yields r = 0.857791, rho = 0.891378 and 8,291 matching signs. The transformation of those displayed values is insufficiently documented to treat that difference as a fitted log2 fold change.

inference.note: S2 prints 13,170 finite raw P and 5,969 finite adjusted P values, all subject to the same site-attribution problem. At raw P < 0.01, there are 135 printed S2 rows versus 73 genes reported in the paper and 93 registered calls. At adjusted P < 0.10 the printed two labels are LOC108352883 and Reln, paired with statistics from unannotated site 10545 and Rgs10 site 3502. Registered edgeR-QL yields zero FDR < 0.05 discoveries. Missing and misattributed author tests remain unassessed. Full-source and jointly finite call counts are in audit.json.

coverage.note: The diagnostic join covers 9,395 of 9,439 registered rows (99.53%) and 9,395 of 13,266 S2 rows (70.82%). Of 44 unpaired registered symbols, 25 lack an S2 row and 19 have duplicate author symbols. In addition to the 40 duplicate-symbol rows, 3,831 unique S2 rows have no registered output. Gene-specific author fitted-effect coverage cannot be established.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use every S2 row, unique case-sensitive symbol matches backed by the same deposited gene ID, and HFD minus chow. Check all six fitted fields, including literal missing-value positions, against every S1 site. Use the journal’s raw P < 0.01 and adjusted P < 0.10, with the project FDR < 0.05 separately. Author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions, at least 30 pairs and 90% relevant coverage, plus both correlations ≥ 0.90 or at least 90% matching directions among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering 90% of pairs. Neither diagnostic establishes valid paired author gene coefficients.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: The accessible S2 worksheet supports a descriptive comparison of the named genes’ normalized expression. Its printed model statistics cannot be attributed to those genes from public evidence. A corrected original fit and library key are required for a direct gene-result comparison specification or verification sign-off.
